questions.question: Does src/engine/engine-types.ts define RawProtocolFact, AcceptedDomainEvent, EngineCheckpoint, EngineOutputEvent, IngestSource/IngestSignal, and PersistenceAdapter as real type definitions and IDB key string constants with no placeholder `any`, no TODO-stubbed field, and no exported type that resolves to `unknown`/`never` as a stand-in for an unfinished shape?

Does src/engine/engine-types.ts contain zero runtime logic beyond type definitions and IDB key string constants (per this story's scope.excludes), keeping engine-types as a pure type-authority module with no behavior a later story could silently depend on?

Could `engine-types` be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its `dependencies_allowed` list (src/domain/* for types and pure helpers only)? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Does src/engine/engine-boundary.structural.test.ts assert, via a grep/AST scan of every .ts file under src/engine/, zero matches for react, next, next/navigation, any src/integration/ path, and any marmot-ts package specifier -- and does the test fail (not silently pass) when a disallowed import is deliberately introduced into a scratch fixture or existing engine file?

Does the shape of RawProtocolFact/AcceptedDomainEvent/EngineCheckpoint/EngineOutputEvent/IngestSignal/PersistenceAdapter authored in engine-types.ts match the field tables in architecture.md's Seam Contracts section field-for-field (name, type, optionality), not just approximately?

Are all IDB key literals (notestr:raw-facts:, notestr:accepted-events:, notestr:engine-checkpoints:, notestr:deferred-ids:) exported as named constants from engine-types.ts rather than inlined as bare strings, so every consumer imports the constant instead of retyping the literal?

does the implementation satisfy AC-BOUND-1's observable -- does a grep-based structural test scanning every .ts file under src/engine/ for import statements matching react, next, next/navigation, src/integration/, or any marmot-ts specifier assert zero matches, and does introducing a single disallowed import (proven, not merely asserted) flip the test from pass to fail?

does the implementation satisfy AC-BOUND-3's observable -- does a grep-based test scanning src/persistence/*.ts and src/engine/*.ts for inlined notestr:raw-facts:/notestr:accepted-events:/notestr:engine-checkpoints:/notestr:deferred-ids: string or template literals outside engine-types.ts assert zero matches, does introducing an inlined duplicate elsewhere flip the test to fail, and is there evidence persistence implementations reference the exported constants rather than retyping the literal?

Does the IngestSignal type exported from engine-types.ts assert full membership over exactly the five variants (message, deferred, skipped, malformed, epoch_advanced) -- no sixth variant, no missing variant -- each with the exact field set from architecture.md's IngestSource/IngestSignal table, and is there a structural/type-level test proving no marmot-ts type appears in any IngestSignal field?

Does the PersistenceAdapter interface exported from engine-types.ts assert the exact eight-method signature set (appendFact, loadFacts, appendAcceptedEvent, loadAcceptedEvents, saveCheckpoint, loadCheckpoint, saveDeferredIds, loadDeferredIds) with the exact parameter/return types from architecture.md's PersistenceAdapter table, and does a test or type-level assertion confirm the idempotency invariants (appendFact idempotent on fact.id; appendAcceptedEvent idempotent on event.id) are encoded as part of the contract rather than left implicit for implementers to guess?

Does the EngineOutputEvent discriminated union exported from engine-types.ts assert full membership over exactly the ten variants (envelope_received, envelope_deferred, domain_event_accepted, domain_event_rejected, projection_invalidated, group_epoch_advanced, group_ratchet_advanced, engine_state_changed, deferred_retry_started, recovered), with no missing or extra variant, matching architecture.md's EngineOutputEvent variant table field-for-field?

When S2 authors src/domain/domain-events.ts, does it import and re-export (or an assignment-compatible generic specialization of) engine-types.ts's forward-declared AcceptedDomainEvent rather than introducing a second, independently-defined AcceptedDomainEvent shape whose fields could silently diverge from architecture.md's Seam Contracts table over time?

Once S4 creates src/persistence/raw-event-log-store.ts, checkpoint-store.ts, and deferred-store.ts, does engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's candidate-file scan (which recursively walks src/persistence/*.ts once the directory exists) actually pick up those new files and correctly flag any inlined IDB key literal in them, without requiring an edit to the test itself?

When S4/S7 wire a real relay event (from applesauce-core or NDK) into RawProtocolFact.nostrEvent, does the runtime value remain structurally assignable to engine-types.ts's locally-declared minimal NostrEvent interface without a cast, or does a field mismatch (e.g. extra required fields, tags typed as a branded array, additional discriminant properties) force one at the marmot-adapter.ts boundary?

engine-boundary.structural.test.ts's import scanner is regex-based (matches `from`/`require(`/`import(` followed by a quoted specifier), not a real TS/AST parser. As S5 (receive-engine.ts) and S6 (ingest-policy.ts) add substantive logic with more import variety, does any legitimate import form slip past the regex undetected (e.g. a re-export statement, a multi-line import, or a specifier assembled via string concatenation rather than a literal), producing a false negative the scanner would miss?

engine-types.ts chose "type" as the discriminant field name for both IngestSignal and EngineOutputEvent — a naming judgment call, since architecture.md's Seam Contract tables list variant names and fields but never name the discriminant key itself. Do S5 (receive-engine.ts, the IngestSignal consumer / EngineOutputEvent producer) and S7 (marmot-adapter.ts, the IngestSignal producer) actually implement against the "type" key as defined here, with no independent reinterpretation that would break the discriminated-union narrowing this file's typing was designed to guarantee?
